mcqs.q: What distinguishes Classical (1750-1820) from Baroque style?
options: A piece six bars long.
Classical means any old serious music.
Use of orchestra (Baroque had none).
Clearer melodic phrases, homophonic texture, balanced structures like sonata form.

mcqs.q: What does the time signature 6/8 indicate?
options: Three notes played at once.
A piece six bars long.
Six beats per bar, all equal in stress.
Two beats per bar, each beat divided into three (compound duple).
Rapid alternation between the written note and the note a step above.
Three notes played at once.
Vibrato on a single note.
Classical means any old serious music.

mcqs.q: In what year did John Cage compose his silent work '4'33"'?

options: Minimalist music uses only one instrument playing one note.
Atonal music is music performed without any rehearsal.
Atonal means the composer chose notes at random with no system.
No - atonal music avoids a key centre but is often rigorously organised; serial works order all twelve pitches in a strict row.

mcqs.q: Does minimalism mean that almost nothing happens in the music?
options: Serialism means writing music for television serials.
Minimalist music uses only one instrument playing one note.
Minimalist music just repeats one idea identically with no development.
No - minimalist works change continuously through gradual processes such as phasing and additive rhythm built on repeating patterns.

mcqs.q: Is 'serialism' just another word for any dissonant modern music?
options: No - serialism is a specific method ordering the twelve chromatic pitches into a row used in prime, inversion, retrograde and retrograde-inversion forms.
Serialism means writing music for television serials.
Any harsh twentieth-century piece can be called serialist.
Atonal music is music performed without any rehearsal.
